name: Hill-Sachs Lesion
definition: Impaction defect of the posterolateral humeral head produced during anterior shoulder dislocation.

investigations.principle: CT best quantifies humeral and glenoid bone loss; MRI assesses associated soft-tissue injury.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Off-track or large defects may change stabilization surgery strategy.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa/Asthi-Sandhi traumatic phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Impaction defect of the posterolateral humeral head produced during anterior shoulder dislocation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
